learning_objective: 🎯 Feel the adrenaline of outdoor adventure sports, learn about trekking, rock climbing, and river rafting, and understand essential safety guidelines!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: रिवर राफ्टिंग (तेज नदी में नाव चलाना)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Adventure sports are physical activities performed in natural, often rugged outdoor environments involving inherent risk, physical challenge, and mental toughness. Their objectives include building self-confidence, leadership, and emotional resilience.
Popular sports include Trekking across diverse terrains, Rock Climbing using safety harnesses and ropes, River Rafting on white-water rapids, Paragliding, and Mountaineering.
Safety is paramount: always use certified safety equipment (helmets, harnesses, life jackets), check weather forecasts, hire trained guides, carry first-aid kits, and never venture out alone.
Participants must respect nature by preserving fragile ecosystems, carrying back all non-biodegradable waste, avoiding campfires in restricted areas, and respecting local wildlife and cultures.

fun_activity.title: 🎒 The Trekking Survival Checklist
fun_activity.instructions: You are going on a 3-day Himalayan trek. List 5 absolute survival essentials you must pack in your rucksack (like a first-aid kit, whistle, water bottle, thermal layers, and navigation compass)!

exam_tips: 📌 Explain the psychological benefits of adventure sports: overcoming fear, building self-confidence, leadership, and emotional resilience.
📌 Always highlight the 'Leave No Trace' environmental principle when discussing outdoor sports.
📌 Know the specific safety gear required for Rock Climbing (harness, carabiners, helmet, belay device, climbing shoes).
quick_recap: ⭐ Adventure sports connect individuals with nature while pushing their physical and psychological limits.
⭐ River rafting difficulty is classified by international scale rapids ranging from Grade I (easy) to Grade VI (extreme/dangerous).
⭐ Thorough preparation, physical fitness, and respect for nature are rules #1 in any adventure sport.
